key_insight: Chronicle is an explainable transformer that uses full, irregular patient treatment timelines to continuously update pan-cancer risk predictions across multiple outcomes.
clinical_relevance: By learning from hospital-wide longitudinal records, it may help stratify patients more accurately than traditional snapshot-based prognostic tools and support individualized treatment planning.
method: Trained on 53.7 million longitudinal data points from 51,711 patients across 67 cancer types
Operates directly on irregular timelines without imputation
Jointly predicts eight clinical endpoints with built-in explainability
evidence_signal: In the abstract, Chronicle outperformed cross-sectional survival models (C-index 0.84 vs 0.76-0.79), predicted seven adverse event/transfusion endpoints (AUC 0.80-0.92), and generalized to 69,341 patients across Germany, Switzerland, and the United States.
watch_item: Real-world deployment will still require local validation and careful attention to differences in data quality, workflow integration, and model calibration across healthcare systems.
paper_title: An explainable transformer model learning from entire treatment timelines for pan-cancer risk profiling across healthcare systems
